recipes.name: Apricot Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place pork chops in a casserole dish. Combine Russian dressing, apricot preserves, and soup mix in a bowl; pour over chops
Bake in the preheated oven until chops are cooked through, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Apricot Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Apricot pork chops is the perfect recipe for those who like sweet and savory. Tender pork pairs well with the apricot glaze and Russian-style dressing.

review.reviewBody: Pretty good! This recipe tastes surprisingly homey - I think I expected a very exotic flavor. The effect is somewhere between a very subtle barbeque sauce and a fruity teriyaki or sweet & sour. This went together in a minute, and came out perfect in an hour. My family says they could go for this every couple of weeks or so - I'm going to try on boneless skinless chicken thighs, too. ** I used a light catalina dressing, and it didn't lose any flavor.

I never made this recipe as stated, but I really like the idea. I didn't change it too much. What I did was use a pork tenderloin (I use anywhere from a 2-1 lbs but you can go bigger or smaller just adjust the cooking time.) I take a 1/2 tbsp sesame oil and 1/2 tbs Olive oil and warm in a nonstick pan over the stove. I spice the pork loin with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and a few red pepper flakes. Then I brown the pork loin on all sides very quickly. While I am browning I warm up the over to at least 350, mix 1/2 packet onion soup mix, 8 ozs of apricot preserves, and 8-10ozs of french dressing, 1tsp sesame oil, and red pepper flakes. I put the pork loin in a foil lined pan, pour the sauce over it, and then wrap the foil around the pork tight. I cook 2/3 baking time covered, and 1/3 uncovered. Like I said about cooking times you will have to ajust the cooking times to your size pork loin.

I have been making a variation of this recipe for a long time, and it's a hit with my family every time I make it. It is similar to sweet and sour pork, but so much easier, and the sauce is delicious over rice. I use fat-free Catalina dressing and instead of apricot preserves, I use a small can of pineapple tidbits. Sometimes, I add some bell pepper strips. Best of all, I throw it all in the crockpot for 4 hours on high or 8 hours on low. Serve it with packaged fried rice (like Rice-A-Roni) and steamed veggies. Fast, easy, cheap, and good!

This is a really good recipe. I made it almost a directed. I had an 8oz. bottle of Russian dressing so I used that. Also I browned 3 thick cut frozen chops in butter in a pan and seasoned them with salt,pepper,garlic powder and onion powder. I fry chops from frozen because it makes for more tender chops. i baked them for 45 minutes because they were partially dun from the pan frying. Totally awesome recipe. We loved it and will have it again. Thanks for sharing.

This recipe made a great base, but it needed perking up for a little more flavor. I seasoned the chops with salt, pepper and garlic powder first. Then I browned the chops in olive oil, adding a diced onion, and half a finely diced green bell pepper. To the sauce mixture, I added a liberal squeeze of fresh lemon juice, and a little white wine. After adding the mixture to the chops, I baked as directed. And it was absolutely delicious served with rice and steamed broccoli.

This fantastic recipe can be even more delicioso.
Add: green olives (15 -20)
 chopped onion (1/2 to whole sweet onion)
 1 green pepper
 1 red pepper
 mushrooms (as many as you want!)
Saute these veggies in a tad of olive oil for five minutes, then pour them in the sauce; then pour the sauce over the pork. (Make sure your casserole dish is large enough). 
 By the way, this exact same sauce with veggies added to it, is absolutely wonderful over pot roast!
this mixture of russian dressing, apricots, and onion soup mix is even better on meatballs- great to have in a crock pot when you have allot of people over !!
Made these in the crock-pot and served over rice, very good! Subbed 'Savory Herb and Garlic' for the onion soup mix...
Sauce was incredible. Pork chops were dry as they don't need cooking near an hour.

Nice recipe & so easy. The taste is somewhere between sweet & sour and bbq. I added a little orange juice to the mixture and also used a pork roast, not chops. Browned the roast and seasoned with garlic, salt, pepper & a little sage prior to baking in the sauce. I think it would be great to use as a marinade for grilled chicken. Next time I will use as a marinade prior to cooking and grill instead of bake. Thanks for sharing!

This turned out really good. I doubled the recipe making 12 chops. I also took the advise and added 1 chopped onion and 1 sliced bell pepper. I also seasoned the chops with salt and pepper and garlic powder then I browned them in a skillet and tossed everything into my slow cooker for 4 hours. Very tastey and tender, they fell apart.
Easy and very tasty. Will make again. Used boneless pork chops. Used some of the sauce on mashed potatoes. Yummy.
Delish! I've been using this recipe for years - if you can't find Russian dressing, you can sub in Catalina dressing instead.
I made it as is & served it with Baked Diced Sweet Potatoes & Baked Zucchini. TOTAL OUT OF THE PARK HOMERUN!! It's already been added to our rotation...
Our favorite recipe for pork chops.

Excellent! I used Apricot pineapple preserves and found a recipe and made the Russian dressing from scratch and it was very good. My husband even said he loved it. Definitely something that will be made again. ??
I followed the directions exactly and it was delicious! Pork chops were tender and sauce was delicious- not too sweet. Served with broccoli and veggie rice.... yum!

I love the taste of it..I used Catalina dressing since I couldn’t find Russian dressing..it tastes almost like sweet and sour..my 13yr old who’s picky asked what the sauce was and said it’s different..he gave it 2 thumbs up..I didn’t do anything different to the recipe and followed as is..it’s delicious
These pork chops are so good. Another go to recipe. AllRecipes you are making me look good with my dinner guests.
kinda sweet. I feel like the sauce could have used something more. The cook time was a little long and the meat was a bit tough. I'd go a shorter next time, maybe 35 minutes.
